source_text: I click on a band, and I see it highlighted, but what I would like would be for the associated family to be rendered as a decomposition of the band itself, not a separate figure below

reply_text:
㊥ (decomposing the band itself) Understood, and I've sent kimi-1 a corrected spec; it's working on it now. When you click a stage, the band in the main figure will split in place into its family stripes, filling exactly the band's own outline day by day. The panel below goes away. That should work out exactly, because each day's family averages add up to the stage's average, which a test already checks.

㊢ (the rest of the spec) While a stage is open:
- **Legend:** the right-hand column shows that stage's families with their hits, under a header like "ASSURANCE BY FAMILY", in place of the count integral. The count integral comes back when you close it.
- **Hover:** a stripe gives stage, family, date and exact hits.
- **Closing:** clicking the band again, Escape, or "All stages" restores the plain band. Clicking another stage switches to it.

The browser check now has to confirm that the stripes sit inside the band: at three sample days, their summed thickness must equal the band's thickness to within a pixel. It also has to confirm there is no figure below. Kimi will plant a bug to show the check catches it.

㊟ (why the first version missed) My first packet offered "in place, or in a linked panel directly below", and Kimi took the panel. The new spec rules the panel out.

㊢ (tracking) Kimi job `invoke-1790895564187-29931-37801d98`, park `park-980d2a38-…`, 45-minute deadline. When Kimi reports back, I'll look at the screenshots myself before publishing, then tell you to hard-refresh. The R-node bidding run is still going in the background.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (one figure, no overlays) You're right: what Kimi built still shows a single figure until you click. Click a stage band or legend button and that stage's families open in a separate panel below the main figure, one stage at a time. You may be after something different. My guess is that the families should be drawn inside the stage bands of the main figure itself: each band split into thinner stripes in shades of its own colour, for all eight stages at once, so the one picture shows both levels. Is that it?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what "overlay" means here) If that's it, these are the details I'd want settled before re-dispatching:
- **Always or toggled:** are the family stripes always shown, or switched on and off with a "families" toggle, so you can compare with the plain stage view?
- **Hover:** hovering over a stripe would give stage, family, day and exact hits.
- **Which families:** each band keeps its top 8 families plus a grey "other". If that is too busy at main-figure size, the top 3–4 plus other is an option.
- **The click-to-open panel:** dropped, or kept for a closer look at one stage?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (if it looks unchanged) If the page looks exactly like before, even after clicking a band, your browser may be showing a cached copy; a hard refresh would fix that. The published file has the click-to-open version; I fetched it back from the site and ran the browser check on it.
